title: Evaluating and drawing the graph
question: When a true graph is supplied, how is the result scored, and how are the graphs and confidence maps drawn?
plain_summary: Two jobs share this page. If the dataset came with a true graph, Judge.evaluation scores the algorithm's graph (S0) against it, before refinement runs. It reports structural Hamming distance (SHD, the number of edge differences), adjacency precision, recall and F1, using causal-learn's graph tools for PC, FCI, GES and CDNOD and a plain cell-by-cell comparison of the matrix for every other algorithm, so undirected and circle marks are scored differently depending on the algorithm. The revised graph is never scored on the CLI, and the scores are only printed to the console. For drawing, one layout is computed from S0 and reused, so the true, initial and revised graphs are drawn with the same node positions by Graphviz. After refinement, one heatmap per edge type shows how often each pair took that type across the 20 bootstrap resamples.

inputs.what: The true graph, 0/1 matrix with [i, j] = 1 meaning j -> i. Present only when the data come from a dataset folder or the simulator; scoring is skipped otherwise (main.py:289).
S0 as an integer matrix; scored by the cell-by-cell branch, used for the layout and the initial plot.
The algorithm's native result object; scored by the causal-learn branch for PC, FCI, GES and CDNOD.
Picks the scoring branch; also used in plot file names.
If a domain column was used (heterogeneous data), it is removed from the graph before scoring.
Column names: node labels for scoring and drawing.
Columns to draw. On the CLI this is every column (main.py:173).
The 7 frequency matrices from refinement; one heatmap each.
Switches drawing to the per-lag branch and the edge colours.

outputs.what: {'shd', 'precision', 'recall', 'f1'} for S0, only when a true graph exists. Printed as a table; neither CLI report template shows it.
In the cell-by-cell branch with a domain column, the last row and column are cut off and written back into the state (judge.py:253).
S0 as named edge lists from convert_to_edges (main.py:286, and again at :337).

sequence.what: Created at main.py:267, right after the algorithm runs. Keeps the columns to draw, their positions, the output folder and results.bootstrap_probability (still None at this point). The threshold argument (0.95) is stored but not used by the drawing code on this path.

Computes node positions once, from S0. Every nonzero cell counts as a link; the matrix is transposed so the layout graph runs cause -> effect; nodes are labelled with column names, underscores replaced by spaces.
Two-stage layout: ForceAtlas2 (500 iterations), then Fruchterman-Reingold (50 iterations, seed 42). If the fa2_modified package is missing it falls back to networkx's spring layout with seed 42.

Draws one matrix with the shared positions. Called for true_graph.pdf when a true graph exists, then for <ALGO>_initial_graph.pdf (main.py:282-284). It converts the matrix to edge lists and adds each type to a mixed graph: directed, undirected, bidirected, circle-ended and 'associated'. If both directions of a directed pair are present, the second add fails and the pair is redrawn as bidirected. For time-series data it draws one SVG per lag plus a summary instead (main.py:268-275).

Renders the mixed graph with Graphviz. With positions given it uses the 'neato' engine and pins each node. Colours: directed edges dark blue, undirected brown with no arrowheads, bidirected red (orange for time series), circle endpoints green, 'associated' dashed blue. The file extension of the save path sets the output format.

The edge-list format used everywhere downstream. It walks every off-diagonal cell: code 1 at [i, j] gives (j, i), read 'j causes i'; codes 4, 5, 6 and 7 are also listed with the column index first; codes 2 (undirected) and 3 (bidirected) are listed with the row index first. Undirected and circle-circle pairs are sorted and de-duplicated. Indices are replaced by names and returned as a dict with keys all_edges, certain_edges, uncertain_edges, bi_edges, half_certain_edges, half_uncertain_edges, none_edges, associated_edges. The algo argument is not used.

Branch 1, for PC, FCI, GES and CDNOD. Takes the native causal-learn graph from raw_result, drops the domain node if there is one, and turns the true DAG into its equivalence class (a CPDAG) with array2cpdag. SHD comes from causal-learn's SHD class, which also counts wrong endpoints; precision and recall are adjacency-only, so direction does not matter. For FCI the native result is a PAG, compared with the true CPDAG.
Builds a causal-learn graph with an edge i -> j for every 1 at [i, j], then calls dag2cpdag. evaluation passes the true matrix transposed, because the truth uses [i, j] = 1 for j -> i.

Branch 2, every other algorithm. Flattens S0 and the truth and compares them cell by cell. SHD is the sum of absolute differences, so a code-2 cell against a 0 adds 2. Only a code-1 cell can be a true or false positive: any other code (undirected, circle, bidirected) falls into the 'tn' count, so it scores neither as a hit nor as a miss. With revise=True this branch would score only the code-1 cells of the revised graph, but the CLI never calls it that way.
A second instance is created after refinement (main.py:306), so it now holds the bootstrap frequency dict.
Draws S4 as <ALGO>_revised_graph.pdf with the same positions as the initial graph, so the two can be compared by eye. main.py:308 then stores S4's edge lists in results.revised_edges.

One seaborn heatmap per bootstrap layer that has any nonzero cell, saved as <layer>_confidence_heatmap.jpg at 1000 dpi with two-decimal labels. Cell [row i, column j] is the share of resamples with that type between j and i; for 'Directed Edge' it is the share with j -> i, so rows are effects and columns are causes. The 'No Edge' layer is almost always nonzero, so it is almost always drawn. A failure on one heatmap is logged and skipped.

failure_paths.what: If the true graph and the processed data differ in size (for example after preprocessing drops a column), branch 1 indexes names by position in array2cpdag and branch 2 subtracts arrays of different shapes at line 259; either raises, and main.py:292 has no try block.
With a domain column, branch 1 removes the last node of the estimated graph and branch 2 cuts the last row and column, both assuming the domain column is last.
Rendering needs the Graphviz binaries. A render error is not caught at main.py:267-285, so it ends the run before refinement.
Errors on a single heatmap are caught and logged; the report later includes only the heatmap files that exist.

change_here.what: Use one scorer for every algorithm on the integer matrix (any nonzero code counts as adjacency; orientation scored separately), and call it again after refinement to fill results.revised_metrics. Then S0 and S4 are comparable, and across algorithms.
Emit every pair in one orientation convention and carry the source stage and frequency with each edge, so downstream prompts and plots can say where an edge came from.
Add an 'any edge' heatmap (adjacency frequency regardless of type), which is the number the refinement step should really be reading.

findings.text: The same graph scores differently depending on which algorithm produced it. On Linear_Gaussian the single correct undirected edge X2 --- X4 scored SHD 0, F1 1.0 from PC but SHD 1, F1 0 from XGES.
findings.label: code verified

findings.text: The revised graph is not scored on the CLI path: results.revised_metrics is never assigned.
findings.label: code verified

findings.text: Our audits measured what the pipeline does not print: in all 25 completed pass-4b runs the final graph had lower adjacency F1 than the algorithm's own graph.
findings.label: code verified

findings.text: The repo's benchmark code scores the algorithm's output and never calls the refinement stage. Which graph the paper's Table 2 scores is a question for the authors.
findings.label: unclear

findings.text: A symmetric mark is stored in one cell only, and which cell depends on the wrapper: PC, GES, GRaSP and FCI mostly above the diagonal, XGES and FGES mostly below. The cell-by-cell scorer and KCI pruning both depend on that choice.
findings.label: code verified

findings.text: Code 7 ('associated') is not counted by the bootstrap tally, so it never gets a heatmap.
findings.label: code verified

findings.text: Our scores use adjacency F1 and distance to the true CPDAG from our own lineage tool, not the pipeline's evaluation; adjacency F1 ignores orientation, which is why the tables also give the CPDAG distance.
findings.label: code verified
